title: Pooled fine count times and terminal photon number have an exact CIR-Poisson quotient

reported_status:
For a scalar f(K), the adjoint generator closes as
  L* f(K) = b(K+m)[f(K+1)-f(K)] + dK[f(K-1)-f(K)],
and the detected-count adjoint is J_t* f(K) = theta c_t K f(K-1). The Hamiltonian term vanishes because it commutes with K. With the Poisson kernel K|S=s ~ Poisson(s/theta), the kernel PGF P_s(z)=exp[(s/theta)(z-1)] intertwines both the number generator and the detected-count map with the CIR generator dS=kappa(m nu-S)dt+sqrt(2 kappa nu S)dW and Cox count likelihood c_t s. The jump identity includes the detected photon subtraction, not only unconditional moments.

Therefore the complete quantum aggregate count record through T together with terminal K has exactly the law of the CIR Cox count record through T and a terminal Poisson(S_T/theta) draw. The equality holds branch by branch under shared record-dependent controls and common classical randomness, while H_t remains number-preserving. The gamma-root coordinates give the conditional physical PGF directly: w(z)=beta theta/(beta theta+1-z), F_K(z|record)=w(z)^m P_J(w(z)). A proved joint TV error epsilon for (record,S_T) transfers to (record,K) with the same epsilon and no quartic bridge allowance.

title: Chemical-state-negative filtering proposes a product-qualified ribosomal display library
status_authority: Current scientific acceptance is conferred only by exact version-bound substantive internal review overlays; physical acquisition and novelty are separate.
reported_status: The source proposes encoding distinct nonstandard peptide products on separate mRNA templates, using established ribosomal elongation and mRNA-display linkage, then applying a downstream chemical-state-negative filter to a completed genotype-linked library. In its example, an uncyclized hydrazinoester product retains an exposed hydrazinyl nitrogen that can react with aldehyde, while the desired cyclic product has consumed that nitrogen. Marking/removing the linear products could qualify library members before functional selection. The source proposes adapting known hydrazone chemistry to intact mRNA fusions; selective capture in an RNA-compatible environment, fusion survival, side-reaction rates, and false tagging have not been demonstrated. The immobilized aldehyde scavenger is speculative.

RNA compatibility, selective chemistry, distinguishable decoding registers and integrated performance remain open. The 22% substrate example is not the double-ring experiment.

title: An empty-carrier signal aliases productive transfer and hydrolysis in the stated assembly states
status_authority: Current scientific acceptance is conferred only by exact version-bound substantive internal review overlays; physical acquisition and novelty are separate.
reported_status: For upstream 3'-O-acylated DNA donor U-O-CO-P_n, the listed productive transfer to a downstream aminated adaptor and hydrolysis of the acyl linkage both leave the upstream carrier in state U-OH. A downstream polymerase that senses only U-OH cannot distinguish the two outcomes. Thus donor-empty is not, by itself, a completion certificate. The failure is observational: an adequate next-address rule must also read a product-qualified receiving state, or the hydrolysis leakage must be separately bounded for the intended use.

proof_availability.classification_scope: Exact indistinguishability of two supplied transition alternatives under the sole empty-donor observation. Product occupancy on the receiving carrier separates this pair, but no reaction rate, physical sensor, chemical identity guarantee or implemented assembler is established.
